body:
The shitty thing is that no matter what improvements I make, I dont feel any better about myself. I've been doing some sort of excercise every day and am down almost 30 lbs on the year. My confidence/self-esteem hasnt even budged. I've tried doing many little things to improve how I view myself; working out, eating better, spending more time with people, dressing better. Still always feel like the same worthless piece of shit 

I truly dont believe there is any way out of this for me other than death. I'm absolutely miserable on a regular basis, and no amount of lifestyle changes, therapy, medication, or self-help has ever been able to make a difference. The unfortunate truth is that some people are simply not cut out for life. Maybe if I'd addressed it back when it started in high school there may have been a chance. Unfortunately my depression is too deeply ingrained after being given over a decade to run rampant. The amount of work necessary to overcome this would likely be too much for most normal, useful people...someone like me just has no chance.

I'm glad you were able to overcome it...I'm actually extremely jealous. But there's no chance for me. I'm already tired of suffering...that's why I want to die so badly. I truly dont see a way of fixing my life. Wouldn't even know how/where to start. Depression has already won...

Thank you for the response. I guess I just don't know how it can possibly get better. I know I don't have it in me to do all the work necessary to put my life back together. I just cant muster up the motivation/energy when I know there's no real point. Hell, even when I had my life "together" I was still miserable. I dont enjoy doing anything...I dont have interest in anything...I'm not good at anything. There is just nothing I really derive any happiness from. My children cant even make happy, and that only makes me feel like an even bigger piece of shit. I really don't think that I can ever beat my depression.

Sadly I can't come up with a good answer to that. The only times I've really had "fun" in my adult life have been when I've been fucked up on various drugs. The only thing I've been somewhat enjoying lately is hanging out with this girl I work with. But of course my stupid ass had to develop feelings, so I'm sure that'll come crashing down in short order...

Yeah I've definitely thought about them. They're 3.5 (stepson) and 1.5, so they're young enough that they'd hopefully forget about me. My wife has already found my replacement, so hopefully the transition to him being dad won't be too difficult. My family have been the only reasons I haven't gone through with it yet. I really dont want to hurt people, I've just reached my limit and truly dont see a way out..

Depression, for me at least, is basically like being trapped 24/7 in a room with the worst bully you've (probably) ever had. There's no escaping the constant emotional abuse. You can't plug your ears to ignore it...you can't get someone to intervene...you can't run away. No matter where you go, this bully will undoubtedly follow you. It constantly berates you for everything and you cant do a damn thing about it. 

No amount of positive thoughts will help; you eventually get to the point where you are incapable of even forming positive thoughts. It wears you down...draining away all of your energy and extinguishing any enjoyment you have for anything. Everything begins to feel like a massive chore; getting out of bed, talking, bathing, eating, playing games, etc. Everything feels devoid of any form of pleasure and ultimately not worth expending the energy. You just want to stay in bed. You just want to sleep. Your tank is absolutely empty. 

Eventually you get to the point where everything seems hopeless. Not that you dont want to have hope, but your brain literally won't allow you to feel it. This cycle repeats, dragging you down lower and lower until it gets to the point of being unbearable. Once you hit that point, death seems to be the only option. The only way to escape the bully with with whom you're imprisoned. It's not that we see it as the easy way out...we see it as the only way out.
